name: epoll_wait
synopsis: int epoll_wait(int epfd, struct epoll_event *events, int maxevents, int timeout);
int epoll_pwait(int epfd, struct epoll_event *events, int maxevents, int timeout, const sigset_t *_Nullable sigmask);
int epoll_pwait2(int epfd, struct epoll_event *events, int maxevents, const struct timespec *_Nullable timeout, const sigset_t *_Nullable sigmask);
description: The epoll_wait() system call waits for I/O events on the epoll instance referred to by the file descriptor epfd and returns them in a buffer up to maxevents. It blocks until an event occurs, is interrupted by a signal, or the timeout expires.

parameters.name: epfd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the epoll instance

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: Pointer to a buffer to store the returned events

parameters.name: maxevents
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return, must be greater than zero

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Timeout in milliseconds; -1 for indefinite blocking, 0 for non-blocking

return_value.success: Returns the number of file descriptors ready for I/O, or zero if the timeout expires
return_value.failure: Returns -1 and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: epfd is not a valid file descriptor
The memory area pointed to by events is not accessible with write permissions
The call was interrupted by a signal handler before events occurred or timeout expired
epfd is not an epoll file descriptor, or maxevents is less than or equal to zero

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.37, a timeout value larger than approximately LONG_MAX / HZ milliseconds is treated as -1 (i.e., infinity).
versions: Linux 2.6, glibc 2.3.2 for epoll_wait; Linux 2.6.19, glibc 2.6 for epoll_pwait; Linux 5.11 for epoll_pwait2
